tool.name: RADAR-PD Utility: Refine in GSAS-II
tool.description: open a RADAR-PD GPX checkpoint in the native GSAS-II desktop
tool.command: touch '$session_log' && trap "chmod a+r '$edited_project' '$session_log' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true" EXIT && set -euo pipefail && python -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; head = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()[:2]; sys.exit(0 if len(head) == 2 and head[0] == 0x80 else "The selected dataset is not a GSAS-II GPX project. Choose a checkpoint from RADAR-PD 5 | GSAS-II handoff projects.")' '$gpx_project' && export GSASII_SOURCE_PROJECT='$gpx_project' && export GSASII_OUTPUT_PROJECT='$edited_project' && /opt/gsasii-gui/start.sh > >(tee -a '$session_log') 2> >(tee -a '$session_log' >&2)

param.name: gpx_project
param.label: GSAS-II project to refine
param.help: Choose one checkpoint from RADAR-PD 5 | GSAS-II handoff projects, or a project saved by this tool. Generic binary support is limited to curated RADAR-PD checkpoint names because NDIP may store collection members as binary.

validator.message: Select a RADAR-PD GSAS-II checkpoint such as Main phase anchor or Accepted model after pass, not a plot or NPZ sidecar.

param.validator: value is not None and (value.name.lower().endswith('.gpx') or value.name.lower().startswith(('01_imported_pattern_and_main_phase', '02_main_phase_anchor', 'accepted_model_after_pass_', 'gsas-ii project ready for interactive handoff', 'gsas-ii refined project')))

tool.help:
Opens a writable copy of one RADAR-PD GPX checkpoint in the native GSAS-II desktop through the browser. The selected input remains unchanged. Every stable save is copied back to **GSAS-II refined project** in Galaxy History, including when the interactive session is stopped from NDIP.
Typical workflow:
1. Run **RADAR-PD Analyze** and expand **RADAR-PD 5 | GSAS-II handoff projects**. 2. Select the final or preferred GPX checkpoint here and run this tool. 3. Open the interactive display, refine parameters in GSAS-II, and use **File > Save project**. 4. Close GSAS-II or stop the interactive job. Continue later by selecting the resulting **GSAS-II refined project**.
This is the full GSAS-II GUI, not the batch GSAS2 refinement tool. Use GSAS-II's own controls for phase fractions, lattice and profile terms, atomic coordinates, occupancies, displacement parameters, background, and instrument parameters. Refining many correlated parameters at once can destabilize a fit; save checkpoints as you proceed.
